meta.subtitle: A loss-making 3D-printing turnaround: revenue stabilizing after divestitures, cost base cut, but cash still burning

analystSentiment.commentary: 3D Systems is a loss-making additive-manufacturing company whose revenue has fallen every year since FY21, from about $0.6B to $386.9M in FY25 ({- -12.1% -} YoY). The recent quarter shows the decline flattening: Q2'26 revenue of $94.6M was {- -0.3% -} YoY, and six-month revenue of $190,117 thousand rose {+ $739 thousand +} on the prior-year period. The clearer shift is on cost. The six-month loss from operations narrowed to $(17,285) thousand from $(52,113) thousand as SG&A fell {+ 20.8% +} and R&D fell to $19,607 thousand from $37,044 thousand after the 2025 Restructuring Plan and two divestitures. FY25 net income of $29.9M is not a return to profitability; it rests on the $125.7 million pre-tax gain from the April 2025 Geomagic sale, against a full-year operating margin of -24.8%. The balance sheet holds a slim net-cash position (net debt of -$5.3M) and a current ratio of 3.40, but free cash flow was -$97.8M in FY25 and consensus still models losses through FY27E. At $3.59 the shares sit near the top of a $1.70-$4.12 52-week range, and my scenarios weight to roughly fair value; I rate the stock HOLD.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
3D Systems Corporation provides 3D printing and digital manufacturing solutions, including 3D printers for plastics and metals, print materials, software, and services such as maintenance and advanced manufacturing. It was founded in 1986, is headquartered in Rock Hill, South Carolina, and describes more than 35 years of additive-manufacturing experience.

Management organizes the business around two industry verticals: Healthcare Solutions, which includes dental, medical devices, personalized health services and regenerative medicine; and Industrial Solutions, which includes aerospace, defense, transportation and general manufacturing. Its technologies include stereolithography, selective laser sintering, direct metal printing and bioprinting, and its software offerings include the 3D Sprint platform.

For revenue reporting the company presents a single consolidated segment, and the available data breaks out no product or geographic revenue mix, so no segment or regional split is quoted here. FY25 revenue was $386.9M. The company serves customers across the medical, dental, aerospace, automotive, industrial and other markets through a direct sales force, channel partners and distributors.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: 3D Systems is a turnaround in progress, not a growth story. After four years of falling revenue and an operating margin of -24.8% in FY25, management has cut the cost base through the 2025 Restructuring Plan and sold two Industrial Solutions businesses, and the six-month operating loss has narrowed sharply. Revenue has roughly stabilized, with Q2'26 down only {- 0.3% -} YoY. The counter-case is that the company still does not make money or generate cash: free cash flow was -$97.8M in FY25, consensus expects losses through FY27E, and the reported FY25 profit came from the Geomagic gain rather than operations. At $3.59 the market already reflects much of the self-help; the probability-weighted value sits close to the current price while the bear case dwarfs the thin upside, so I see no directional edge and rate the stock HOLD.

catalysts: Continued reduction in the operating loss: the six-month loss from operations narrowed to $(17,285) thousand from $(52,113) thousand a year earlier, and management does not expect significant additional 2025 Restructuring Plan charges in 2026.
Stabilizing top line: Q2'26 revenue of $94.6M held roughly flat year over year, helped by product-revenue growth on higher printer volume in the dental and medical technology markets.
A return toward revenue growth as modeled by consensus, with FY27E revenue of $410.5M.
Tariff recoveries: approximately $2.6 million was recovered in the second quarter of 2026, supporting gross profit.
risks: Persistent cash burn: free cash flow stayed negative in FY25 and consensus models continuing losses through FY27E.
Customer concentration: two Healthcare Solutions customers were 12.2% and 11.4% of FY25 revenue.
Further impairments: the company recorded $145.0 million of impairments in 2024 and $302.8 million in 2023, and warns more could follow.
Convertible-note obligations: the 0% 2026 Notes and the 5.875% 2030 Notes carry covenants and settlement demands on limited liquidity.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue has declined in each of the last four years, from about $0.5B in FY22 to $386.9M in FY25, a {- -12.1% -} drop in the latest year. Gross margin has compressed alongside, from 42.8% in FY21 to 33.9% in FY25.

The current year shows the erosion slowing. Q2'26 revenue was $94,579 thousand versus $94,838 thousand a year earlier, a change of {- $(259) thousand -}, or {- 0.3% -}. Product revenue rose to $54,842 thousand from $53,801 thousand on higher printer volume in the dental and medical technology markets, while service revenue fell to $39,737 thousand from $41,037 thousand on lower recurring service revenue and divestitures. Six-month revenue of $190,117 thousand was {+ $739 thousand +} above the prior-year period.

Cost discipline is the clearer story: six-month SG&A fell {- $17,425 thousand -}, or 20.8%, and R&D fell to $19,607 thousand from $37,044 thousand, cutting the six-month operating loss to $(17,285) thousand from $(52,113) thousand. Gross profit margin was 36.4% in Q2'26 against 38.1% a year earlier, held back by unfavorable mix from higher printer sales and partly offset by about $2.6 million of tariff recovery.

Reported FY25 net income of $29.9M and diluted EPS of $0.19 do not signal a profit engine; they rest on the $125.7 million pre-tax gain from the April 2025 Geomagic sale, against a FY25 operating margin of -24.8%. On a trailing-twelve-month basis the operating margin was -15.8% and the net margin -14.2%.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
The balance sheet has thinned over the cycle but is not stretched. Cash and short-term investments fell from $0.8B in FY21 to $0.1B in FY25, and total equity fell from $0.8B to $0.2B over the same span.

Total debt was $90.3M at FY25, and with cash on hand the company held a slim net-cash position, net debt of -$5.3M. Liquidity remains adequate: the FY25 current ratio was 2.87 and the trailing-twelve-month current ratio 3.40, down from 5.80 in FY21.

The financing overhang is the convertible debt named in the filing: the 0% convertible senior notes due 2026 and the 5.875% convertible senior secured notes due 2030, whose covenants restrict additional debt and certain investments and whose settlement or repayment the company must fund. Net debt to EBITDA is quoted at 0.9x, but with negative trailing EBITDA that multiple carries little signal.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash generation is the weakest part of the story. Free cash flow was negative in four of the last five years and was -$97.8M in FY25, a FCF margin of -25.3%. Operating cash flow was negative in FY25, and capital expenditure was modest at -$9.9M. The trailing-twelve-month FCF yield was -8.8%.

Despite the burn, the company repurchased $15 million of stock in FY25 and pays no dividend. Divestitures have supplied non-operating cash: the Geomagic sale closed in April 2025 for $119.4 million in cash, and the 3DXpert and Oqton sale closed in October 2025 for $3.3 million in cash plus a royalty receivable with a present value of $7.1 million. Those proceeds cushion liquidity but do not fix the underlying cash burn.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
Conventional earnings multiples are not usable here because the company loses money. Trailing P/E is -16.3x and EV/EBITDA -13.8x, and the forward P/E on next-twelve-month estimates is -25.6x; the FY27E consensus still carries an EPS loss of $-0.13. The one positive-signed multiple is price-to-sales at 1.5x.

The Street is split: four analysts carry two Buys and two Holds with no Sells and no aggregate consensus rating, and the consensus price target is $5.50 (a range of $5.00 to $6.00), about {+ 53.2% +} above the current $3.59. That target implies a re-rating toward growth and breakeven that the reported numbers have not yet delivered, which is why I anchor valuation on scenarios rather than a single multiple.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Revenue returns to growth toward the FY27E consensus of $410.5M, the cost reductions from the 2025 Restructuring Plan carry the business to operating breakeven, and the shares re-rate to the $5.50 consensus target as losses give way to positive EBITDA.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue holds near the FY26E consensus of about $393.4M (+2%), losses narrow but persist, and the stock stays range-bound near the current $3.59 as the market waits for sustained free-cash-flow generation.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Revenue decline resumes as key customers pull back, cash burn continues against FY25 free cash flow of -$97.8M, and refinancing of the 2026 and 2030 convertible notes pressures the equity; the shares retrace toward the lower half of the $1.70-$4.12 range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The three scenarios span a wide outcome set because the business is near breakeven on operations but still burning cash.

The Bull case matches the Street's consensus target and assumes the FY27E revenue of $410.5M arrives with the lower cost base intact. The Base case keeps the shares close to today's price, consistent with FY26E revenue of about $393.4M and continued but shrinking losses. The Bear case sits {- 41.5% -} below the current price and reflects a return to revenue decline, ongoing negative free cash flow, and the refinancing demands of the convertible notes.

I weight the Base case at 50%, the Bear at 30% and the Bull at 20%, which leaves probability-weighted value close to the current price. The thin upside does not offset the far larger bear-case downside, so the shares look fairly valued with no directional edge, which supports a HOLD rather than a directional call.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The company reports revenue as a single consolidated segment and discloses no product or geographic revenue split, so no percentage mix is quoted. Management describes two industry verticals within it. Healthcare Solutions covers dental, medical devices, personalized health services and regenerative medicine, and is where the two customers that were 12.2% and 11.4% of FY25 revenue sit; recent product-revenue growth came from higher printer volume in the dental and medical technology markets. Industrial Solutions covers aerospace, defense, transportation and general manufacturing, and was the source of the Geomagic divestiture completed in April 2025 and the 3DXpert and Oqton divestiture completed in October 2025.

moatFactors.name: Proprietary materials and IP
moatFactors.body: The majority of materials used in the company's 3D printers are proprietary, and it has more than 35 years of additive-manufacturing experience. That materials-attach model has not prevented gross margin from falling from 42.8% in FY21 to 33.9% in FY25, so the pricing power it implies is limited.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: End-to-end digital workflows plus maintenance and software contracts create some stickiness, but Q2'26 service revenue fell to $39,737 thousand from $41,037 thousand a year earlier on lower recurring service revenue, showing the installed base is not defending revenue.

moatFactors.name: Customer concentration
moatFactors.body: The two Healthcare Solutions customers noted in the segment, one of which was 16.0% of revenue in 2024, concentrate demand and receivable credit risk; concentration of this kind is a source of risk, not advantage.

moatFactors.name: Scale and cost position
moatFactors.body: Revenue has fallen every year since FY21 to $386.9M, and operating margin was -24.8% in FY25; the company has lacked the scale to cover its cost base, which is why the 2025 Restructuring Plan was needed.

businessMoat.durability: The competitive position is not durable on the current numbers. Revenue has declined for four straight years and gross margin has kept compressing, the signature of a business without pricing power in its end markets. Proprietary materials, a large installed base and long experience give the company something to build on, but they have coincided with, not prevented, persistent operating losses and negative free cash flow. The recent cost cuts and divestitures make the company smaller and leaner rather than structurally advantaged. Until revenue growth and positive free cash flow return together, I treat the moat as absent.

points: Consensus models a return to growth: FY26E revenue of about $393.4M (+2%) and FY27E revenue of $410.5M, above FY25's $386.9M.
Product revenue is the growth line today, rising to $54,842 thousand in Q2'26 from $53,801 thousand a year earlier on higher printer volume in dental and medical technology markets.
Six-month revenue grew {+ $739 thousand +}, an early sign the multi-year decline may be flattening after divestitures.
Personalized healthcare services and parts manufacturing were cited as areas of growth within an otherwise declining service line.
Estimates still embed losses: FY26E EPS of $-0.14 and FY27E EPS of $-0.13, so growth is expected in revenue before it reaches the bottom line.

management.leadership: The proxy names Dr. Jeffrey A. Graves as President, Chief Executive Officer and Director. The finance seat turned over in the past year: Phyllis Nordstrom was appointed permanent Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Administrative Officer on March 23, 2026, having served as Interim CFO from August 20, 2025, after Jeffrey Creech resigned his CFO role effective August 29, 2025. Other named executive officers for 2025 are Reji Puthenveetil (EVP, Additive Solutions and Chief Commercial Officer), Joseph Zuiker (EVP, Engineering and Operations) and Charles Hull (EVP, Chief Technology Officer). A CFO change during a turnaround adds execution risk, though the permanent appointment removes the interim overhang.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation has centered on shrinking and de-risking the portfolio. The company completed two divestitures from Industrial Solutions, Geomagic in April 2025 for $119.4 million in cash, and 3DXpert and Oqton in October 2025 for $3.3 million in cash plus a royalty receivable valued at $7.1 million, and executed the 2025 Restructuring Plan to lower the cost base. It repurchased $15 million of stock in FY25 and pays no dividend. Buying back stock while free cash flow ran at -$97.8M is a questionable use of cash for a company that also must fund convertible-note settlements; I would rather see the proceeds retained until operations generate cash.
management.governance: Governance rests on the DEF 14A filed April 8, 2026. Eight of the nine director nominees are independent under NYSE standards; Dr. Graves is not independent because he is an executive officer. One related-party relationship is disclosed: director nominee Dr. Vasant Padmanabhan is an executive officer of Smith+Nephew, a customer that bought software and on-demand services in 2023, 2024 and 2025, with aggregate value below $1 million each year on arm's-length terms, and the Board determined he had no material interest. The compensation program uses an independent compensation committee and advisor, a clawback policy, stock ownership guidelines, double-trigger change-in-control agreements, and caps of 150% of target on annual bonuses and 200% on performance-share units. The forward-looking disclosures also flag the company's need to remediate material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, which is a governance concern to watch.
management.insiderOwnership: As of March 23, 2026, all executive officers and directors as a group (14 persons) beneficially owned 5,841,883 shares, or 3.99% of the common stock. Dr. Graves held 1,035,117 shares and Charles Hull 924,385. Among the directors, Kevin S. Moore held 1,690,310 shares, or 1.16%. Outside holders dominate the register: State Street Investment Management held 7.78%, BlackRock 6.56% and Bank of Nova Scotia 5.19%. Insider ownership is modest relative to these institutions, which limits management's direct equity alignment but is not unusual for a company of this size.

idiosyncratic: Cash burn and financing: FY25 free cash flow was -$97.8M and the trailing-twelve-month FCF yield -8.8%, while the balance sheet carries $90.3M of total debt including the 0% 2026 convertible notes and the 5.875% 2030 convertible notes, whose covenants restrict additional borrowing and whose settlement the company must fund from limited cash.

Customer concentration: two Healthcare Solutions customers were 12.2% and 11.4% of FY25 revenue, and one represented 16.0% in 2024 and 15.0% in 2023; losing either would materially hit revenue and create concentrated receivable credit risk.

Impairment history: the company recorded $145.0 million of impairments to goodwill and long-lived assets in 2024 and $302.8 million of goodwill impairment in 2023, and warns a declining share price and market capitalization could trigger further tests.
Revenue visibility: hardware sales are back-end-loaded within quarters and tied to a lengthy, uneven selling cycle, so a slip in large-printer orders can swing reported revenue in any period.

Turnaround execution: reported FY25 profit depended on the $125.7 million Geomagic gain, not operations, and a CFO transition during the restructuring raises the risk that cost savings do not translate into sustained positive cash flow.
risks.systemic: The 10-K risk factors emphasize macroeconomic and geopolitical exposure: inflation that remains uneven across regions, interest rates that are moderately elevated by historical standards, and tightening credit conditions that can reduce customers' ability to finance equipment purchases. Trade policy and tariffs are a two-way factor; the company recovered about $2.6 million of tariffs in Q2'26, but changes in trade relations could raise sourcing costs or disrupt distribution. As a capital-equipment supplier to cyclical end markets such as aerospace, defense, automotive and general manufacturing, the company's demand is sensitive to industrial capital spending, and foreign-exchange swings move reported revenue given its Americas, EMEA and APAC footprint.

body: I rate 3D Systems HOLD with a target range of $3.00 to $4.50, bracketing a base case of $3.75 against the current $3.59. The investable improvement is real: the six-month operating loss has narrowed sharply as the 2025 Restructuring Plan lowered SG&A and R&D, and Q2'26 revenue was down only {- 0.3% -} YoY. But the company still lost money at the operating line, burned -$97.8M of free cash flow in FY25, and depends on a re-rating that consensus prices at $5.50 yet the fundamentals have not earned.

The setup is balanced rather than directional. The Bull case needs revenue growth to the FY27E $410.5M with the new cost base intact; the Bear case at $2.10, {- 41.5% -} below the current price, needs revenue decline to resume against continued cash burn and convertible-note refinancing. With the base case near today's price and probability-weighted value close to it, the reward does not compensate for the downside, so I would wait for two or three quarters of positive free cash flow before paying up.
